abstracts.value: We present results over an 11-year Solar cycle of cosmic antiprotons based on <math display="inline"><mn>1.1</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></math> events in the rigidity range from 1.00 to 41.9 GV. The <math display="inline"><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover></math> fluxes exhibit distinct properties. The magnitude of the <math display="inline"><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover></math> flux temporal variation is significantly smaller than those of <math display="inline"><mi>p</mi></math>, <math display="inline"><msup><mi>e</mi><mo>-</mo></msup></math>, and <math display="inline"><msup><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></math>. A hysteresis between the <math display="inline"><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover></math> fluxes and the <math display="inline"><mi>p</mi></math> fluxes is observed, whereas the <math display="inline"><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover></math> and <math display="inline"><msup><mi>e</mi><mo>-</mo></msup></math> fluxes show a linear correlation. With a model-independent analysis, we found a universal relation between the shape of the rigidity spectrum and the magnitude of flux temporal variation over an 11-year Solar cycle for both positively and negatively charged particles. The simultaneous results on <math display="inline"><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover></math> and <math display="inline"><mi>p</mi></math>, <math display="inline"><msup><mi>e</mi><mo>-</mo></msup></math>, and <math display="inline"><msup><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></math> provide unique information for understanding particle transport in the Solar System as a function of mass, charge, and spectral shape.
